name: Dirty Martini Dip

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper, plus more for garnish

instructions.primary_message: Drain and quarter the pitted Spanish Queen olives lengthwise. Drain the jarred diced pimentos. Bring the cream cheese to room temperature. Bring the crème fraîche to room temperature. Crumble the blue cheese.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅔ cup pitted Spanish Queen olives
2 tbsp jarred diced pimentos
226 g cream cheese
½ cup crème fraîche
85 g blue cheese, preferably gorgonzola dolce

instructions.primary_message: In a 2-cup glass jar, place olives, jarred pimento, lemon peel strips, gin, vermouth, and 3 tablespoons olive brine; seal and shake until combined. Refrigerate until flavors meld for at least 30 minutes and up to 1 day.
Using a fine-mesh strainer set over a bowl, strain olive mixture, reserving olives and pimentos in a separate bowl from marinade; discard lemon peels.

In the bowl of a food processor, place cream cheese, crème fraîche, gorgonzola dolce, salt, pepper, 2 tablespoons reserved gin marinade, 1 tablespoon oil, and remaining 2 tablespoons olive brine and process until smooth, about 1 minute, stopping to scrape down sides of bowl as needed.
Add 1/3 cup of reserved drained olives and pimentos, and pulse until finely chopped and incorporated into cream cheese mixture, 8 to 10 (1-second) pulses.
Transfer mixture to a medium serving bowl, cover, and refrigerate until flavors meld and dip is slightly thickened, about 30 minutes.
Before serving, drizzle with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and top with remaining 1/3 cup olives and pimentos. Garnish with black pepper. Serve with crudités, potato chips, or crackers.

missing: pitted Spanish Queen olives, drained and quartered lengthwise

schema_metadata.keywords: Dirty Martini Dip, Martini Dip Recipe

description: This briny, cheesy dip is inspired by the dirty martini—olives, pimento, blue cheese and all.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 15 min.

Optional or for serving: Crudités, potato chips, and/or crackers, for serving

Notes: While we prefer to use gorgonzola dolce for its creamier texture and sweeter flavor, any blue cheese will work in this recipe.

Make-ahead and storage: The dip can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
author: Leah Colins
